text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- More Airbus apologies likely: Ottawa expected to admit error in including Moores and Schreiber in letter.
- Ailing Yeltsin back in hospital: Doctors detect pneumonia.
- India says terrorists get aid in Canada: Funds being sent to Sikh groups.
- Ottawa wants to trim different kind of fat: Exercise guide aimed at improving fitness standards of a greying population.
- Former WHL executive sexually abused players: League never censured or investigated man who also owned Portland team.
- WIC beats back back breakup bid: Thwarts surprisingly strong showing by dissident shareholders to dissolve the company.
- Will Loewen's victory be too costly: Battle with SCI has analysts wondering if funeral home group can continue 'torrid pace of acquisition'
- Robert Friedland in the hunt for Chinese diamond properties: May end up with stake in VSE firm.
- Dollar rises above 74 cents: Central bank intervenes after bullish forecasts fuel demand.
- Slap in face for WIC board: Minority shareholders show displeasure by voting to dissolve company. But controlling families kill motion.
- Antitrust fears pushed SCI to drop Loewen bid.
